autocorrect/maximum attempts.description:
Set to 0 to turn off autocorrect.
An attempt is every stroke from the first keypress to the next full release.
Recommended to turn off when you are comfortable using Quickfix.
autocorrect/maximum attempts.name: maximum attempts

chording/concatenation style.description:
Appended (classic) places spaces directly after a chord. Recommended for typists.
Prepended places spaces lazily between two chords. Recommended for text editing and coding.
chording/concatenation style.name: concatenation style

chording/detection method.description:
In latency (classic) mode each key is printed instantly and backspaced after a successful chord.
Smart adds a small amount of latency depending on your tolerances,
and only prints characters when it is no longer plausible for the inputs to be a chord input.
Continuous (spurring) and allows you to jump from one chord to the next
without releasing all keys, with more potential speed traded against the flexibility of
character entry.
chording/detection method.name: detection method

chording/minimum chord keys.description: A minimum chord key count of 1 can very slightly affect typing latency.
chording/minimum chord keys.name: minimum chord keys

chording/press tolerance.description: Scales with the number of chord inputs.
chording/press tolerance.name: press tolerance

chording/release tolerance.description: Scales with the number of chord inputs.
chording/release tolerance.name: release tolerance

fuzzy modifiers/press theshold.description: The time between a modifier press and the previous key press
fuzzy modifiers/press theshold.name: press theshold

fuzzy modifiers/release guard threshold.description: The time between a modifier press and a subsequent key press that prevents the next modifier release from affecting it.
fuzzy modifiers/release guard threshold.name: release guard threshold

fuzzy modifiers/release theshold.description: The time between a modifier release and the previous key press
fuzzy modifiers/release theshold.name: release theshold

gaming/layer warp.description: Re-press held keys with new layer mappings when switching layers.
gaming/layer warp.name: layer warp

keyboard/command control swap.description: Swaps CTRL and ⌘ to make transitioning between Mac and other systems easier.
keyboard/command control swap.name: command control swap

keyboard/rollover.description:
How many keys can be held at once and still be detected by your PC, excluding modifier keys.
Older hardware or especially BIOS/UEFI might only support 6-key rollover.
This only affects reporting to the host system, CCOS always uses full n-key-rollover.
Requires a replug to be effective.
keyboard/rollover.name: rollover

chording/concatenation style.description:
Appended (classic) places spaces directly after a chord. Recommended for typists.
Prepended places spaces lazily between two chords. Recommended for text editing and coding.
chording/concatenation style.name: concatenation style

chording/detection method.description:
In latency (classic) mode each key is printed instantly and backspaced after a successful chord.
Smart adds a small amount of latency depending on your tolerances,
and only prints characters when it is no longer plausible for the inputs to be a chord input.
Continuous (spurring) and allows you to jump from one chord to the next
without releasing all keys, with more potential speed traded against the flexibility of
character entry.

Older hardware or especially BIOS/UEFI might only support 6-key rollover.
